messages:
maya: heads-up — seeing sustained p95 latency regressions in us-west1 dedicated pool for the last ~20m. looks correlated with a flood of small requests that keep hitting max-batch and holding pack windows open. SLO misses started around 1918208800. cc @sre-oncall @ryan :eyes:
ryan: can you paste the grafana panels and any counters? queue/admission and max_batch_reached?
maya: grafana here: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/pool-us-west1 (p95 spike shown). logs + counters: ```[2026-03-18T17:30:12Z] pool=us-west1 node=gpu-12 admission_queue=78 max_batch_reached=1 pack_window_ms=40 prefill_kv_rate=120/s
[2026-03-18T17:31:02Z] pool=us-west1 node=gpu-12 admission_queue=95 max_batch_reached=1 pack_window_ms=40 prefill_kv_rate=130/s```
maya: interestingly max_batch_reached increment is sticky (counter keeps flipping true for longer windows) — looks like continuous batching pressure, not one-off burst.
tess: we've seen this pattern before — admission hysteresis + aggressive prefill can keep the admission gate closed too long, causing tails to build even when raw QPS dips. hysteresis is preventing quick re-opening.
victor: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce pack_window_ms from 40 -> 20 for the us-west1 dedicated pool; 2) temporarily increase max_batch_size from 1024 -> 1536; 3) throttle background prefill_kv jobs. any preference? :thumbsup:
sre-oncall: please pick one low-risk change and we can roll it immediately. we want minimal config churn. also capturing incident.
ryan: I'll do a canary of option (1) on 3 nodes (gpu-12, gpu-14, gpu-19) and monitor for 10m. running: ```./infra ctl set-config --pool us-west1 --pack_window_ms 20 --node-list gpu-12,gpu-14,gpu-19 --reason "mitigate max_batch stickiness 1918209999"```
infra-bot: rollout initiated by ryan (rollout_id=roll-20260318-0723). canary nodes: gpu-12,gpu-14,gpu-19. watching health checks.
ryan: canary applied. watching admission_queue, p50, p95 and cpu. initial 2m: p95 dropped from ~420ms -> ~160ms on canary nodes, admission_queue depth reduced ~40%.
maya: good signal. what about cost/CPU?
ryan: CPU on canary nodes increased ~6% and vram usage flat. small cost impact but within burst buffer.
victor: if (1) holds we can roll to pool, but schedule a follow-up to revert pack_window to adaptive behavior — long-term we want hysteresis to be workload-aware. also need to throttle prefill_kv jobs — they're contributing to steady small requests.
tess: long-term fixes: - adaptive admission thresholds by observed seq-lens and QPS - rate-limit background prefill to windows outside peak - add a circuit-breaker to avoid sustained max_batch_reached boolean (decay window)
sre-oncall: filing incident: INC-2026-0318-03. mitigation (pack_window -> 20) rolled to pool after canary at 1918210500. will keep incident open for postmortem.
maya: after pool-wide roll p95 across pool dropped from 420ms -> 130ms within 8m. SLOs back within margin. leaving mitigation in place for now.
ryan: created PR to make pack_window adaptive: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/482 (WIP). also adding a toggle for prefill_kv throttle.
victor: note: increasing max_batch_size is a heavier change (impacts memory / kernel choices) — prefer pack_window tweak + prefill throttle as medium-term.
tess: assigning follow-ups: @ryan own adaptive admission RFC, @maya run eval for prefill throttle impact on cache hit rate, @victor coordinate perf regression tests for changing max_batch_size.
maya: thanks team. will update incident timeline and collect traces for postmortem. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
